feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid platform/operations expertise. It reads professionally and is mostly polished, but it would be stronger with tighter structure, fewer repeated skill sections, and more quantified outcomes beyond responsibilities.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level positioning: the headline, summary, and career progression align well with digital strategy/communications leadership roles.  
- Strong credibility: recognizable employers, large-scale website migration, analytics stack, and cross-channel ownership all signal real depth.  
- Writing is generally clear and professional, with effective use of action verbs and concrete tools/platforms.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” “Technical + IT,” and “Soft Skills” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and scannability.  
- Add more impact metrics: several bullets describe duties rather than outcomes. Include measurable results such as engagement growth, email performance, efficiency gains, revenue/support impact, or adoption improvements.  
- Fix minor style/consistency issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12 years of experience”; maintain consistent comma usage in lists (e.g., “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “web, email, social and multimedia”); “A2/Learning” is stylistically awkward—use “A2 (learning)” instead.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear positioning, but it’s slightly generic and repeats themes covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and anchoring it more explicitly in recent leadership scope will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and grammar.
- Lead with your current value proposition: digital strategy, platform modernization, and operational systems for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Replace broad lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) with a sharper phrase like “multi-channel digital communications.”
- Consider a tighter rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience building and leading multi-channel programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in digital strategy, platform modernization, editorial operations, and cross-functional workflow design. Strong track record translating policy and technical subject matter into clear, audience-focused content that supports advocacy, engagement, and organizational goals.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows/systems” are repeated in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy messaging” and “stakeholder coordination” also appear elsewhere; keep the intro higher-level.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value, recent capabilities will make it sharper and more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with more senior, specific language: “Multi-channel communication” → “Cross-channel communications leadership”; “Web & CMS administration” → “CMS modernization & web operations.”
- Prioritize strategic and current strengths: digital transformation, editorial governance, analytics, platform/workflow architecture, advocacy communications, and multimedia production.
- Use parallel noun phrases for consistency and polish.
- Suggested version: Digital transformation & communications strategy • Cross-channel communications leadership • CMS modernization & web operations • Editorial governance & workflow design • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Workflow architecture & systems improvement • Stakeholder & cross-functional coordination • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” repeats the header and Soft Skills almost exactly.
- Several items overlap with Topline Skills; consider using this section only for broad themes, leaving tools/platforms to later sections.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the project footer and prior NACo entries. Tighten around strategic ownership, platform impact, and 1–2 concrete outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper lead: “Lead digital strategy, platform modernization, and content operations for a U.S. national membership organization in a full-time freelance engagement.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4 focused points: enterprise systems/analytics, Drupal campaign builds, cross-channel governance, and AI-enabled search leadership.
- Replace generic phrasing like “support,” “advise,” and “deliver” with stronger verbs: “lead,” “design,” “build,” “standardize,” “optimize.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, users served, workflow time saved, publishing speed improved, search/discovery gains, toolkit downloads, or stakeholder teams enabled.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search initiative” and Drupal microsite work duplicate the Recent Projects section; keep this entry higher-level and let the footer hold examples.
- “Governance, usability, and operational best practices” overlaps with prior NACo roles; emphasize what is new or more senior here.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-scope leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management points covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad lead sentence with a sharper scope/outcome summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Reorder bullets to lead with highest-impact achievements: website migration, analytics stack expansion, in-house studio build, governance/operations.
- Make channel leadership more outcome-based: add email open/click growth, social engagement/follower growth, video output, cost savings, or production volume if available.
- Tighten phrasing for concision, e.g. “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ publishers.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; differentiate this role as enterprise leadership, budget, systems, and modernization.
- Video leadership also appears in earlier NACo roles; emphasize building the studio and scaling in-house production capacity here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like support than leadership. Tighten it to emphasize scope, channel ownership, and systems/process impact distinct from the later director role.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to show ownership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Make bullets parallel and outcome-oriented:
- Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Coordinated editorial planning across communications, advocacy and program teams to improve alignment and publishing cadence.
- Standardized digital publishing workflows to improve consistency, speed and cross-team coordination.
- If possible, add metrics: open rates, video views, publishing volume, turnaround time, or number of teams/stakeholders supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; differentiate this entry as scaling/formalizing the program.
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered more strategically in the 2022–2024 director role.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership

Suggested edit
- Replace broad terms with sharper, leadership-level language: “Enterprise digital strategy” → “Enterprise digital communications strategy”; “Audience-focused content planning” → “Audience and journey-based content strategy.”

- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Editorial systems and governance” duplicates “Digital governance & editorial systems” in Core Competencies.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with multiple recent role bullets; avoid repeating exact phrasing elsewhere.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:

- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery

- Workflow automation

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads as a generic tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities tied to modernization and delivery rather than listing every platform.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery”
- Remove lower-signal or dated items here, especially “jQuery,” unless it is required for target roles.
- Put the strongest, most recent differentiators first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations/automation.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “Enterprise CMS modernization for high-volume public-sector sites”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates the “Technical + IT” section; keep Topline Skills strategic and let Technical + IT hold the full tool list.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies and the header summary; avoid repeating the exact phrase verbatim.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

- Power BI

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps with “Data analytics & reporting” in Core Competencies and repeats tools already validated in the 2022–2024 role.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from software list to capability + outcome language, e.g.: “Analytics strategy, KPI frameworks, executive dashboards, user behavior analysis, SEO/performance insights.”
- Tighten and group tools: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity” rather than separate bullets if space is tight.
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with stronger phrasing like “executive reporting” or “decision-ready reporting.”
- Consider a rewrite: “Analytics strategy & optimization — GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity; KPI design, executive dashboards, user-behavior analysis, SEO/performance optimization.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “KPI design” and “reporting” partially duplicate “Data analytics & reporting” in Core Competencies.
- Tool names here duplicate the NACo Director role; keep this section concise and let the work entry carry proof/impact.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skills item is relevant, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps with the broader “Multimedia & live event production” competency. It would be stronger if framed around delivery scope and recent leadership-level capability shown in the NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic nouns with sharper, outcome-oriented skill phrasing: “Broadcast-quality video production,” “Livestream and hybrid event delivery,” “PTZ camera and studio system operation.”
- Add a leadership/ownership angle to match recent roles: “In-house studio buildout and operations” or “End-to-end multimedia production.”

- Broadcast-quality video production & editing
- Livestream, hybrid & virtual event delivery
- PTZ camera systems & multi-camera workflows
- Studio buildout, operations & run-of-show production

- “Studio operations” and “Hybrid and virtual event production” are already implied by recent work experience; avoid repeating them elsewhere verbatim.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and partially duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/current platforms or add light proficiency context.

Suggested edit
- Prioritize most relevant/current tools first: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider “Drupal (enterprise, migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- If space allows, add level/scope rather than just names: e.g., “Drupal (enterprise CMS, migrations, modular content) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- Keep phrasing platform-focused only; avoid adding modernization, APIs, or workflow language here since those are covered elsewhere.
- If Drupal is your clear flagship platform from recent roles, make that explicit by leading with it and adding a qualifier.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same platforms.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel minor compared with enterprise CMS experience; cut it if you need space or want a more senior emphasis.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support your recent Drupal/CMS modernization work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as execution-focused tools, e.g.: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group operational tools separately: “Technical integrations & deployment: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, GitHub Actions, Cloudflare Workers”
- If accurate, add scope/outcome context in brief parentheticals, e.g. “Google Tag Manager (tracking deployment), GitHub Actions (build/deployment automation)”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the rest of the CV uses that style; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing
- If Cloudflare Workers or GitHub Actions were materially used in recent roles, mention them in a recent experience bullet instead of relying only on the skills list

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. Given the stronger, more recent experience in systems architecture and digital operations, this item should emphasize automation/building platforms over basic collaboration tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Systems
- Reorder by relevance/strength: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams
- Remove lower-value or older-feeling tools unless central to target roles: Basecamp, Trello
- If accurate, add light qualifiers to show depth, e.g. “Airtable (workflow/database systems) • Power Automate (Microsoft 365 automation) • Zapier (cross-platform integrations)”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear under Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same language here.
- Slack/Teams/Asana overlap with general coordination skills, so keep only if they support a systems/operations positioning.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful platform list, but it’s too bare to show level of ownership or strategic relevance. Since recent roles emphasize email operations and enterprise communications, this item should signal campaign/CRM capability rather than read like a generic software list.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing, CRM & Member Engagement Systems
- Rewrite as: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers: enterprise email automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation, member communications
- Best upgrade: move one concrete outcome into recent experience instead of here, e.g., newsletter scale, automation improvements, or engagement/reporting gains

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with Work Experience entries already covering email leadership; avoid repeating “managed newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here
- If Dynamics 365 was central in recent consulting work, consider mentioning it there for stronger impact than in skills alone

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize “firsts,” production scope, and team-building contributions.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to stress foundational impact: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and establish workflows for web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add clearer ownership and outputs: “Supported a major website refresh; produced livestreams and a recurring weekly video update; coordinated day-to-day digital production across channels.”
- Tighten the management line: “Provided day-to-day supervision and training for a digital media associate.”
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience reach, publishing volume, or efficiency gains from workflow improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; here, frame it as launching/building the format rather than expanding it.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats later roles; in this older entry, position it as helping establish baseline processes.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia work, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it shorter, emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator, and tie the research/project work to organizational impact if possible.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; helped translate findings into digital and multimedia content.”
- Make the podcast launch the second sentence and tighten phrasing: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- If possible, add a measurable outcome: number of episodes, audience growth, internal adoption, or how it expanded NACo’s communications capabilities.
- Remove generic wording like “contributed to digital content production” unless you can specify formats or purpose.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this item focused on research support + first podcast launch.
- Avoid repeating broad web/email/social responsibilities already covered in 2015–2024 roles.
